lecture_notes.title: Introduction to Robot Motion Planning
lecture_notes.content: Robot motion planning involves determining a sequence of valid configurations that moves a robot from a start position to a goal position. Key concepts include configuration space, obstacles, path planning, and feasibility. Understanding these basics is essential for designing effective robotic systems.

lecture_notes.title: Motion Planning Algorithms
lecture_notes.content: Common motion planning algorithms include the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT), Probabilistic Roadmap (PRM), and A* search. These algorithms help robots find collision-free paths in complex environments. Each algorithm has strengths and limitations depending on the application context.

lecture_notes.title: Robot Control Principles
lecture_notes.content: Robot control principles focus on how to execute planned motions accurately. Basic concepts include feedback control, PID controllers, and trajectory tracking. These principles ensure the robot follows the planned path despite disturbances or uncertainties.

lecture_notes.title: Application in Construction Robotics
lecture_notes.content: Construction robotics applies motion planning and control to automate tasks such as material handling, assembly, and inspection. Challenges include dynamic environments, safety, and precision. Integrating planning and control enables robots to operate effectively on construction sites.

worked_examples.title: Planning a Path Using A* Algorithm
steps: Define the grid environment with obstacles and free spaces.
Set the start and goal positions on the grid.
Calculate the cost for each node using the A* heuristic.
Expand nodes by selecting the one with the lowest cost.
Continue until the goal node is reached.
Trace back the path from goal to start.

worked_examples.title: Implementing a PID Controller for Robot Arm Movement
steps: Identify the desired position and current position of the robot arm.
Calculate the error as the difference between desired and current positions.
Apply the PID formula: control signal = Kp*error + Ki*integral(error) + Kd*derivative(error).
Adjust the robot arm actuators based on the control signal.
Repeat the process to minimize error and achieve smooth motion.

worked_examples.title: Applying Motion Planning in a Construction Scenario
steps: Model the construction site environment including obstacles and work areas.
Select an appropriate motion planning algorithm (e.g., RRT) for path generation.
Plan a collision-free path for the robot to transport materials.
Use control principles to follow the planned path accurately.
Monitor and adjust the plan as needed for dynamic changes.

exercises.title: Define Key Concepts of Robot Motion Planning
exercises.prompt: Explain the terms configuration space, path planning, and obstacle avoidance in robot motion planning.

exercises.title: Describe Motion Planning Algorithms
exercises.prompt: Compare the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and Probabilistic Roadmap (PRM) algorithms in terms of their approach and typical applications.

exercises.title: Explain Robot Control Principles
exercises.prompt: Describe how a PID controller helps a robot maintain its trajectory during motion.

exercises.title: Apply Motion Planning to Construction Robotics
exercises.prompt: Given a simplified construction site layout, outline a strategy to plan and control a robot to move materials safely and efficiently.

exercises.title: Solve a Simple Motion Planning Problem
exercises.prompt: Using a grid map with obstacles, find a path from start to goal using the A* algorithm and explain each step.
